modules.title: Knife System & Construction
modules.summary: Read the knife as one system: cutting geometry, steel structure and hand interface.

content.lead: Accurate explanations start with accurate names.
points: Tip, spine, blade face, heel and cutting edge describe different parts of the blade.
The cutting edge, or edge, is the sharpened boundary; the bevel narrows the blade toward the apex.
Surface finish describes appearance or texture, not the underlying cross-section.
content.takeaway: Name the feature before explaining what it does.

content.lead: Tang type, bolster design and forging describe how a knife is made, not a universal quality score.
points: Full, hidden, through and partial tangs are distinct handle constructions.
A bolster can be integral or joined as a separate component.
Forging shapes solid steel by deformation; stock removal shapes it mainly by removing material.
content.takeaway: Construction terms answer how; quality depends on execution and intended use.

content.lead: Handle materials change feel, stability, moisture response, care and appearance.

modules.title: Steel Performance Foundations
modules.summary: Understand steel as a set of interacting performance dimensions rather than a prestige number.

content.lead: Knife steel is best understood through several properties that pull in different directions.
points: Hardness resists indentation and supports a thin edge under load.
Toughness resists cracking and fracture under impact or lateral stress.
Edge retention, corrosion resistance and ease of sharpening complete the practical picture.
content.takeaway: A steel profile is multi-dimensional.

question.prompt: Which statement best describes a knife steel?
question.explanation: A steel profile is multi-dimensional.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: Which statement best describes a knife steel?
recovery_questions.explanation: A steel profile is multi-dimensional.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Know the five performance dimensions: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: A steel profile is multi-dimensional.

content.lead: Hardness and toughness answer different failure questions.
points: A hard edge can resist deformation but may tolerate less abuse if other factors are unfavorable.
A tough steel can resist fracture without necessarily holding a fine edge longest.
Geometry and heat treatment strongly influence how these properties appear in use.
content.takeaway: Hard is not the same as tough.

question.prompt: Which property most directly resists cracking?
question.explanation: Hard is not the same as tough.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: Which property most directly resists cracking?
recovery_questions.explanation: Hard is not the same as tough.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Separate hardness from toughness: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: Hard is not the same as tough.

content.lead: Long edge life, corrosion resistance and easy sharpening do not always rise together.
points: Wear-resistant carbides can support edge retention but can raise sharpening effort.
Stainless steels resist corrosion better, but stainless does not mean stain-proof.
The useful balance depends on food, maintenance habits and sharpening access.
content.takeaway: Choose the profile that fits the user, not the maximum value.

question.prompt: What can high wear resistance change?
question.explanation: Choose the profile that fits the user, not the maximum value.

recovery_questions.explanation: Choose the profile that fits the user, not the maximum value.

recovery_questions.explanation: Choose the profile that fits the user, not the maximum value.

questions.explanation: A steel profile is multi-dimensional.

questions.explanation: Hard is not the same as tough.

modules.title: Metallurgy, Heat Treatment & Steels
modules.summary: Connect composition, microstructure, steelmaking route and heat treatment to practical behavior.

content.lead: Alloying elements modify hardenability, carbide formation, corrosion resistance and other behaviors.
points: Carbon is central to hardness and carbide formation.
Chromium supports corrosion resistance and can also form carbides.
Vanadium, molybdenum and tungsten can contribute to carbide behavior and high-temperature performance.
content.takeaway: Composition sets possibilities; it does not finish the steel.

question.prompt: Which element is strongly linked to corrosion resistance in stainless steel?
question.explanation: Composition sets possibilities; it does not finish the steel.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: Which element is strongly linked to corrosion resistance in stainless steel?
recovery_questions.explanation: Composition sets possibilities; it does not finish the steel.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Know what alloying elements change: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: Composition sets possibilities; it does not finish the steel.

content.lead: Heat treatment develops the microstructure that makes a steel specification useful.
points: Austenitizing, quenching and tempering control hardness and structure.
Carbide type, size and distribution influence wear resistance and edge behavior.
Grain control and retained austenite also affect practical performance.
content.takeaway: The same alloy can behave differently after different heat treatment.

question.prompt: What most directly develops the final microstructure of a blade steel?
question.explanation: The same alloy can behave differently after different heat treatment.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: What most directly develops the final microstructure of a blade steel?
recovery_questions.explanation: The same alloy can behave differently after different heat treatment.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Understand heat treatment and carbides: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: The same alloy can behave differently after different heat treatment.

content.lead: Steelmaking route influences carbide distribution and cleanliness, but the route is not a quality guarantee by itself.
points: Powder metallurgy can produce fine, even distributions in highly alloyed steels.
Conventional steels can perform extremely well when composition, processing and heat treatment are appropriate.
Xinzuo steel choices should be compared by actual specification and intended use, not by category labels alone.
content.takeaway: Process route is one variable in the whole steel system.

question.prompt: What does powder metallurgy guarantee by itself?
question.explanation: Process route is one variable in the whole steel system.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: What does powder metallurgy guarantee by itself?
recovery_questions.explanation: Process route is one variable in the whole steel system.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Distinguish conventional and powder metallurgy: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: Process route is one variable in the whole steel system.

modules.title: Damascus & Blade Construction
modules.summary: Distinguish layered construction, visible pattern and functional claims.

content.lead: The word Damascus can describe different constructions that should not be treated as identical.
points: Core-and-cladding Damascus uses a cutting core with patterned layered cladding.
Full pattern-welded Damascus uses layered material through the blade section rather than only as outer cladding.
Historical crucible-pattern steels are a different metallurgical route.
content.takeaway: Name the construction before discussing the pattern.

question.prompt: What does core-and-cladding Damascus contain at the cutting core?
question.explanation: Name the construction before discussing the pattern.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: What does core-and-cladding Damascus contain at the cutting core?
recovery_questions.explanation: Name the construction before discussing the pattern.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Distinguish Damascus constructions: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: Name the construction before discussing the pattern.

content.lead: A visible pattern shows appearance or construction evidence, but it does not by itself prove cutting performance.
points: Layer count is not a universal quality score.
Laser or surface decoration can imitate a Damascus-like pattern without layered construction.
Cutting performance still depends on edge steel, heat treatment and geometry.
content.takeaway: Pattern is evidence to interpret, not a performance certificate.

question.prompt: What can a Damascus-like laser pattern prove?
question.explanation: Pattern is evidence to interpret, not a performance certificate.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: What can a Damascus-like laser pattern prove?
recovery_questions.explanation: Pattern is evidence to interpret, not a performance certificate.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Separate pattern from performance: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: Pattern is evidence to interpret, not a performance certificate.

content.lead: Layer combinations can be designed so different constituents wear at different rates.
points: Differential wear can create microscopic texture as layers respond differently during use or sharpening.
That mechanism does not mean a knife literally sharpens itself forever.
Geometry, hardness contrast and real use determine whether the effect is useful.
content.takeaway: Describe the mechanism precisely and avoid magical claims.

question.prompt: What is a careful description of differential-wear full Damascus?
question.explanation: Describe the mechanism precisely and avoid magical claims.

recovery_questions.prompt: Review: What is a careful description of differential-wear full Damascus?
recovery_questions.explanation: Describe the mechanism precisely and avoid magical claims.

recovery_questions.prompt: Application check — Understand differential wear claims: which answer is correct?
recovery_questions.explanation: Describe the mechanism precisely and avoid magical claims.

questions.explanation: Name the construction before discussing the pattern.

questions.prompt: Module check — Separate pattern from performance: which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: Pattern is evidence to interpret, not a performance certificate.

questions.prompt: Module check — Understand differential wear claims: which answer is correct?
questions.explanation: Describe the mechanism precisely and avoid magical claims.

modules.title: Geometry & Bevels
modules.summary: Understand how the blade approaches the apex and how geometry changes cutting behavior.

lessons.title: Know bevel, edge bevel and apex

content.lead: Near the cutting edge, several geometric features perform different jobs.
points: The primary grind thins the blade toward the cutting region.
The edge bevel is the narrow facet immediately beside the apex.
A microbevel is a deliberately small additional edge bevel.
content.takeaway: Sharpen the intended edge geometry, not every visible surface.

content.lead: Single- and double-bevel knives distribute sharpening geometry differently.
points: Double bevel means both sides are sharpened, not necessarily a perfect 50/50 ratio.
Traditional single bevel concentrates the main working bevel on one side.

content.lead: Cutting feel depends on more than the edge angle.

Distal taper changes mass, stiffness and penetration toward the tip.

modules.title: Knife Types, Balance & Ergonomics
modules.summary: Choose knife families from the work, then compare balance and fit in the user's hand.

content.lead: Chef's knife, gyuto, santoku and thin Chinese cleavers can all cover broad kitchen work with different emphasis.
points: Longer chef and gyuto profiles offer reach and versatility.
Santoku gives a compact all-round format with useful blade height.
A thin Chinese cleaver is not automatically a heavy bone cleaver.

content.lead: Specialist knives solve narrow mechanical tasks with specific geometry.

Fillet knives may use designed flexibility to follow fish contours.

modules.title: Cutting Technique & Safe Use
modules.summary: Use the right movement on a stable workstation and keep force aligned with the cut.

content.lead: Different profiles and foods favor different controlled movements.
points: Push cutting moves the edge forward and down through food.
Rocking uses a curved edge with a controlled pivoting motion.
Long slicing uses edge length in a smooth draw through the food.
content.takeaway: Choose the motion that fits blade profile and task.

question.explanation: Choose the motion that fits blade profile and task.

lessons.title: Stabilize board, food and supporting hand

content.lead: Many accidents begin before the blade starts moving.
points: Stabilize the board and create a stable face on rolling food.
Set the supporting hand before the knife moves and keep fingertips out of the blade path.
Unexpected resistance is a reason to stop and diagnose, not simply add force.
content.takeaway: Stable board. Stable food. Clear path. Hidden fingertips.

lessons.title: Avoid lateral load and unsafe handling

content.lead: Kitchen knives are cutting tools, not levers or hidden objects in a sink.
points: Do not twist a thin hard blade free when it binds; withdraw and change the cut.
Do not scrape sideways with the cutting edge when the spine or a scraper can do the job.
Keep knives visible and controlled during washing, passing and carrying.

modules.title: Maintenance & Cutting Boards
modules.summary: Protect the edge and materials through suitable surfaces, cleaning, drying, storage and inspection.

content.lead: Every cut ends with contact between the edge and the cutting surface.
points: Suitable wood, purpose-made plastic and resilient synthetics can be appropriate cutting surfaces.
Glass, ceramic, stone and metal are too hard for routine contact with fine edges.
Stability, hygiene and maintenance matter alongside edge friendliness.
content.takeaway: Judge a board by what it does to the edge and the work environment.

points: Wash promptly by hand with mild cleaning and rinse away salt or acids.
Dry blade and handle completely before storage.

modules.title: Sharpening Foundations & Diagnosis
modules.summary: Prepare a stable stone, control edge-bevel contact, reach the apex, remove the burr and verify the result.

content.lead: Sharpening starts with a suitable, wetted, flat-enough and stable abrasive surface.
points: Follow the stone manufacturer's soaking or splash-and-go instructions.
Flatten excessive dishing before serious sharpening.
Use a holder or damp support that does not slide or rock.
content.takeaway: Stable stone first, edge work second.

question.prompt: What should you do if the stone support moves?

lessons.title: Control bevel contact along the full edge

content.lead: The main sharpening skill is maintaining local edge-bevel contact from heel to tip.
points: Use marker to see where the stone removes material on the edge bevel.
Adapt hand position as the blade profile curves rather than freezing the wrist.
Work heel, middle, curved front and tip; do not overwork only the center.
content.takeaway: Coverage and contact matter more than counting strokes.

lessons.title: Use the burr as evidence, then remove it

Reduce pressure and alternate sides to weaken and remove the burr.

levels.title: Intermediate
levels.purpose: Apply the same domains to realistic trade-offs, customer needs and cause-effect relationships.

modules.title: Knife System & Construction
modules.summary: Read the knife as one system: cutting geometry, steel structure and hand interface.

content.lead: At intermediate level, construction must be interpreted through loads, ergonomics and manufacturing choices.
points: A welded bolster is neither good nor bad by itself; fit, joint quality, heat control and finishing matter.
Tang mass and handle material shift weight distribution and perceived balance.
Forging can be useful when material must be redistributed, but it does not replace good heat treatment or geometry.
content.takeaway: Judge the design as a system, not one construction keyword.

question.prompt: A production knife has a welded bolster. What can you conclude from that fact alone?

options.text: The knife must have been forged in one piece
The joint and total execution still have to be evaluated
The balance point is fixed by the bolster alone

question.explanation: A welded bolster is a construction choice; quality depends on the joint, heat control, finishing and the complete design.

recovery_questions.prompt: A hidden-tang knife is proposed for normal kitchen work. Which judgement is technically sound?

options.text: A hidden tang is always weaker than a full tang
A hidden tang is suitable only with wooden handles
Durability depends on tang dimensions, fit, fastening and expected loads
Tang style alone determines the knife's balance

recovery_questions.explanation: Tang labels do not determine durability by themselves; dimensions, assembly and the expected load path matter.

recovery_questions.prompt: What is the most defensible reason to prefer forging in a particular knife design?

options.text: It can redistribute solid steel into a useful shape before finishing
It always produces a thinner edge

recovery_questions.explanation: Forging is a manufacturing route that can redistribute material; it does not replace heat treatment, grinding or geometry control.

questions.prompt: The same blade is fitted with a much denser handle material. What is the most likely user-visible change?

options.text: The edge angle becomes more acute
Weight distribution and perceived balance can move toward the handle

questions.explanation: Handle mass is part of the knife system and can change balance and perceived handling without changing the blade steel.

options.text: The knife must have been forged in one piece
The joint and total execution still have to be evaluated
The balance point is fixed by the bolster alone

questions.explanation: A welded bolster is a construction choice; quality depends on the joint, heat control, finishing and the complete design.

options.text: A hidden tang is always weaker than a full tang

modules.title: Steel Performance Foundations
modules.summary: Understand steel as a set of interacting performance dimensions rather than a prestige number.

content.lead: Intermediate judgement connects property trade-offs to actual work and maintenance habits.
points: A user who sharpens rarely may value retention differently from one who maintains edges often.
Thin geometry increases cutting efficiency but can reduce abuse tolerance independently of steel name.

Make both bevels perfectly symmetrical regardless of original design
Choose the lowest angle the sharpener can hold
Restore sufficient integrity while preserving the knife's intended section and use

questions.explanation: Repair should solve the damage without unnecessarily redesigning the knife.

questions.prompt: A knife consistently steers to one side after sharpening. Which geometric cause should be checked first?

options.text: Bevel or section asymmetry creating unequal cutting forces

questions.explanation: Steering is a directional symptom, so asymmetry is more relevant than unrelated finish variables.

questions.prompt: After years of sharpening, the apex is sharp but the knife wedges much more than when new. What diagnosis fits best?

options.text: The apex is necessarily too polished
The handle has shifted the balance point forward
The blade may have become too thick behind the edge and need controlled thinning
The steel has automatically lost toughness

questions.explanation: Repeated sharpening can move the edge into a thicker part of the blade even when the apex itself is sharp.

modules.title: Knife Types, Balance & Ergonomics
modules.summary: Choose knife families from the work, then compare balance and fit in the user's hand.

content.lead: Advanced recommendation resolves cases where task fit, perceived balance, fatigue and user technique point in different directions.
points: High-volume repetitive work can make small differences in reach and balance more important.
A user's natural grip can change leverage enough to reverse a first impression of balance.
A sound recommendation explains why one compromise fits this user better rather than declaring a universal best knife.
content.takeaway: Explain the fit decision in terms of the user's actual work.

question.prompt: A cook likes a knife during a short trial but develops fatigue during long prep. What should be reassessed?

options.text: Reach, grip, balance and repetitive-load ergonomics over the real work cycle
Only the knife's measured center of mass
Only whether the shape is traditional

question.explanation: Long-duration fit can reveal leverage and fatigue effects that a short first impression misses.

recovery_questions.prompt: Why can a user's natural grip reverse an initial impression of balance between two knives?

options.text: Grip position changes leverage and how mass is felt around the hand
The physical center of mass changes permanently
The blade steel changes density during use
The handle becomes lighter when pinched

recovery_questions.explanation: Perceived balance is relational: the same fixed mass distribution can feel different from different grips.

recovery_questions.prompt: Two knives solve the task, but one is more agile while the other is more stable through long cuts. What is the advanced recommendation approach?

options.text: Declare the heavier knife universally better
Choose the harder steel regardless of movement
Use price as the deciding technical variable
Explain the trade-off against the user's actual workflow and let that determine fit

recovery_questions.explanation: Advanced recommendation makes the compromise explicit instead of pretending there is one universal best configuration.

Tradition associated with the knife type

questions.explanation: Ergonomics matters after the tool is mechanically appropriate for the work it must perform.

modules.title: Cutting Technique & Safe Use
modules.summary: Use the right movement on a stable workstation and keep force aligned with the cut.

content.lead: Advanced technique analysis connects observed damage to movement, load direction, food stability and geometry.
points: Repeated lateral scraping can damage a fine apex without any problem in steel quality.
Twisting a bound blade creates lateral stress that can chip or fracture hard thin sections.
A good diagnosis changes technique or tool choice before changing material specification.
content.takeaway: Trace damage back to the load that created it.

question.prompt: Microchips appear mainly after twisting cuts. What is the first corrective action?

options.text: Remove the lateral twisting load and reassess the cutting method
Increase the sharpening angle before checking technique
Use more downward force to finish the cut

question.explanation: The damage correlates with lateral loading, so the first correction is to remove that load.

recovery_questions.prompt: A fine edge is repeatedly used to scrape food sideways across the board. What failure mechanism becomes more likely?

options.text: Lateral loading and abrasion at the apex unrelated to normal slicing
Loss of heat treatment through room-temperature friction

recovery_questions.explanation: Side scraping loads the fine apex in a direction it is not optimized to support.

recovery_questions.prompt: A blade repeatedly binds in the same dense ingredient. What should be changed before specifying a tougher steel?

options.text: Technique, entry angle, food support or tool choice

recovery_questions.explanation: A recurring load created by technique or tool mismatch should be corrected before changing material specification.

questions.prompt: Damage appears only during one particular movement, while the same edge survives other work. What is the best diagnostic clue?

options.text: The load direction and resistance created by that movement

questions.explanation: A symptom that tracks one motion strongly implicates the load path of that motion.

modules.title: Maintenance & Cutting Boards
modules.summary: Protect the edge and materials through suitable surfaces, cleaning, drying, storage and inspection.

content.lead: Advanced care diagnoses whether a problem comes from surface contact, moisture, chemistry, storage or sharpening interval.
points: Rapid dulling on a hard board can mimic poor steel performance.
Localized corrosion patterns can reveal trapped moisture or residue rather than insufficient alloy alone.
Handle movement or cracking should be traced to material, assembly and environmental cycles.
content.takeaway: Diagnose the exposure before blaming the material.

question.prompt: An edge dulls unusually fast only on one workstation. What should be inspected first?

options.text: The board surface and the user's contact habits on that station

question.explanation: A problem isolated to one workstation points first to local contact conditions.

recovery_questions.prompt: Localized corrosion appears where a blade contacts a sheath or guard. What is the leading hypothesis?

The balance point is too far forward
Moisture or residue is being trapped at the contact area

recovery_questions.explanation: The location of the corrosion is evidence about the local exposure condition.

options.text: Material movement, assembly method and environmental cycling

recovery_questions.explanation: Handle movement can come from the interaction between material behavior, assembly and moisture cycles.

modules.title: Sharpening Foundations & Diagnosis
modules.summary: Prepare a stable stone, control edge-bevel contact, reach the apex, remove the burr and verify the result.

content.lead: Advanced sharpening separates dullness, rolling, chipping, geometry thickening and wire-edge failure before choosing an intervention.
points: A knife can feel dull because the apex is damaged or because the blade has become too thick behind the edge.
Repair, reprofiling and thinning remove different amounts of steel and solve different problems.
The intervention should preserve intended geometry and stop once evidence shows the problem is corrected.
content.takeaway: Diagnose first; remove only the steel the problem requires.

question.prompt: The apex is sharp, but a knife wedges badly after years of sharpening. What intervention may be needed?

options.text: A larger burr at the same geometry
Controlled thinning behind the edge rather than more work on the apex
A more polished apex without changing the section

question.explanation: Apex sharpness and behind-edge geometry are different problems and require different interventions.

recovery_questions.prompt: An edge cuts paper immediately after sharpening but loses bite after a few cuts. What should be suspected?

options.text: A residual wire edge or incomplete deburring

recovery_questions.explanation: A wire edge can feel very sharp briefly, then fold or break away because the apex was not properly deburred.

recovery_questions.prompt: What distinguishes chip repair, reprofiling and thinning?

options.text: They are three names for the same sharpening step
They remove steel from different regions to solve different geometric problems
They differ only by the stone brand used
They always require the same final angle

recovery_questions.explanation: Advanced sharpening starts by identifying which part of the geometry is actually causing the problem.

questions.prompt: During a corrective sharpening job, when should steel removal stop?

options.text: After a fixed number of strokes
Only when every scratch from the coarser stone disappears
When evidence shows the diagnosed problem is corrected and intended geometry is restored
When the burr becomes as large as possible

questions.explanation: Corrective work should be evidence-driven and remove no more steel than the problem requires.
